"Cameraman Describes Baldwin as Careful with Firearms on 'Rust' Set; Detective Details Shooting Incident in Affidavit"

Alec Baldwin was described as very careful with firearms on the set of the movie "Rust" by cameraman Reid Russell, according to a search warrant affidavit. However, the affidavit also reveals that assistant director Dave Halls was unaware that the prop gun given to Baldwin contained live rounds.

The affidavit, written by Detective Joel Cano of the Santa Fe Sheriff’s Department, details how the tragic shooting incident occurred during a rehearsal. Director Joel Souza and cinematographer Halyna Hutchins were preparing a scene when Baldwin discharged the firearm.

According to the affidavit, only one bullet was fired, which went through Hutchins and then struck Souza. Hutchins reportedly said she couldn’t feel her legs before receiving medical attention.

The affidavit highlights that the film's crew had issues, including a walkout by seven camera crew members just hours before the incident. Detective Cano noted challenges on the set, such as delays caused by having to find a replacement camera crew.

The spent casing from the fired prop gun was retrieved by the film’s armorer, Hannah Gutierrez, indicating a single shot was fired. Gutierrez stated in the affidavit that she checked the bullets in the gun before giving it to Halls, who then handed it to Baldwin.

Halls said in the affidavit that he did not know the gun was loaded with live rounds and that he should have checked all the rounds himself.

Santa Fe District Attorney Mary Carmack-Altwies and the Santa Fe Sheriff’s Department have announced a joint press conference regarding the investigation.

Baldwin, who is also a producer on the film, has spoken about the incident on Twitter, saying, "There are no words to convey my shock and sadness regarding the tragic accident that took the life of Halyna Hutchins, a wife, mother and deeply admired colleague of ours."

The film's production company, Rust Movie Productions, has halted production and issued a statement saying, "We have halted production on the film for an undetermined period of time and are fully cooperating with the Santa Fe Police Department’s investigation. We will be providing counseling services to everyone connected to the film as we work to process this tragic event."

The incident has once again brought attention to the issue of safety on film sets, particularly when it comes to the use of firearms. The Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) has issued a statement saying, "This is a terrible tragedy and we mourn the loss of our member, Halyna Hutchins. Citigroup's $500 Million Mistake: A Wake-Up Call for Banking UX Design

In a stunning blunder that has shaken the financial world, Citigroup inadvertently transferred $500 million to Revlon's creditors due to an outdated user interface in its wire transfer system. The incident, which has been labeled as one of the biggest banking errors in history, has drawn attention to the critical need for modern and intuitive user experience (UX) design in the financial sector.

Alex Khmelevskiy, the head of UX design at Clay, a leading design agency, criticized Citigroup's system, stating, "This incident underscores the importance of having a user-friendly and error-proof interface, especially in the high-stakes world of banking. The fact that such a massive mistake could occur due to confusion in the system is a clear indication that it's time for an upgrade."

Citigroup, acknowledging the issue, is now working to update its loan operations platform. A spokesperson for the bank said, "We are committed to enhancing our systems and controls to prevent such incidents in the future. In the meantime, we have added significant controls to our processes until the new system is fully operational."

The interface in question is provided by Oracle's Flexcube, a third-party application widely used in the industry for wire transfers. However, Oracle declined to comment on the situation, leaving Citigroup to address the consequences of the procedural failure.

A federal judge, Jesse Furman, recently ruled against Citigroup's attempt to recover the mistakenly transferred funds, stating that the creditors were entitled to keep the money. This decision was based on a legal precedent, which holds that recipients of such payments are not required to return them if they had no reason to suspect the transfer was an error.

Judge Furman expressed hope that the industry would learn from Citigroup's misfortune, emphasizing the importance of minimizing error risks. "This case should serve as a wake-up call to banks and financial institutions to review their processes and ensure they have adequate safeguards in place to prevent similar mistakes," he said.

The error occurred when a subcontractor in India, while setting up the transaction to transfer a $7.8 million interest payment to Revlon, mistakenly checked the wrong boxes on the outdated Flexcube interface. This action triggered the transfer of the full $894 million loan amount instead of the interest payment.

The incident has sparked a broader conversation about the role of technology and user experience in the financial sector. As Khmelevskiy emphasized, "In today's digital age, there's simply no excuse for such complexity and confusion in a system that handles billions of dollars daily. It's time for banks to prioritize user-centered design to ensure the safety and security of their clients' assets."

The suspect has been charged as an adult with four counts of first-degree murder, seven counts of assault with intent to murder, and one count of terrorism.

Eligibility and Requirements

To utilize Venmo's check-cashing feature, users must meet certain eligibility criteria. These include having a verified email address, an active Venmo debit card or direct deposit, and enabling location services on their device.

Partnership and Fees

Venmo has partnered with First Century Bank and Ingo Money to provide this service. As a subsidiary of PayPal, Venmo's check-cashing feature is also linked to its parent company. Notably, Venmo is waiving all fees associated with cashing government stimulus checks, allowing users to access their stimulus money without incurring any deductions.

Fee Waiver and Resumption

Venmo has committed to waiving fees for cashing stimulus checks up to a total of $400,000. Once this threshold is reached, the check-cashing feature will resume normal operations with applicable fees.

Step-by-Step Process

To cash a stimulus check using Venmo, users can follow these steps:

Download the Venmo app on their mobile device.
Verify their account information, including their email address and phone number.
Within the Venmo app, select the 'Cash a Check' option.
Take clear photos of the front and back of the stimulus check.
Venmo will conduct a review process to ensure the funds are available.
Once approved, the check amount will be deposited into the user's Venmo account.

Instant Access and Waiting Period

Venmo offers two options for accessing the deposited funds: instant access or a standard waiting period. Instant access incurs a fee, while the standard waiting period is free. For stimulus checks, the instant access fee is waived.

Tracking and Managing Stimulus Payments

In addition to the 'Cash a Check' feature, Venmo provides users with tools to track and manage their stimulus payments. The app displays the status of the payment, including whether it has been issued, deposited, or cashed.

Potential Third Stimulus Check

While the second round of stimulus payments is currently being distributed, discussions are ongoing regarding a potential third stimulus check. Venmo's 'Cash a Check' feature and other services will be available to facilitate the distribution of future stimulus payments if authorized.

Facebook removed more than 20 million posts for COVID-19 misinformation

Facebook and its photo-service Instagram took down more than 20 million pieces of content containing COVID-19 misinformation between the start of the pandemic and June but couldn't say how prevalent these types of false claims are on the platforms.

The social network measures the prevalence of other types of content such as hate speech and adult nudity because it gives the company a sense of what offensive posts Facebook missed. Providing this metric for COVID-19 misinformation, the company said, is more complex.

"When it comes to COVID, though, things are evolving even more quickly so it does make prevalence even more difficult to define and measure," said Guy Rosen, Facebook's vice president of integrity, during a press conference on Wednesday.

The action came about a month after the White House singled out Facebook in saying that about a dozen people were responsible for creating 65% of the vaccine misinformation on social media platforms -- all of whom remained active on the social networking giant.

Despite the action against "disinformation dozen," the White House continued to criticize Facebook's response to misinformation.

"In the middle of a pandemic, being honest and transparent about the work that needs to be done to protect public health is absolutely vital, but Facebook still refuses to be straightforward about how much misinformation is circulating -- and being actively promoted -- on their platform," a White House spokesperson told CNN Business on Wednesday.

Facebook didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the spokesperson's remarks.

Politicians, including US President Joe Biden, and advocacy groups have criticized social networks for failing to effectively combat the spread of COVID-19 and vaccine misinformation. Facebook partners with fact-checkers, directs people to authoritative information and labels misinformation. But researchers have questioned how effective those measures are in curbing the spread of false claims online.

"There will always be examples of things we missed and, with a scale of our enforcement, there will be examples of things that we take down by mistake," Rosen said. "There is no perfect here."

Facebook said it has more than 65 criteria for false claims about COVID-19 and vaccines that would prompt it to remove posts from its platforms. The company has added to this list, including false claims that COVID-19 vaccines cause Alzheimer's and that being around vaccinated people could cause secondary side effects to others.

The social network said it removed more 3,000 accounts, pages and groups for violating its rules against COVID-19 and vaccines. It has also displayed warnings on more than 190 million pieces of COVID-related content on Facebook that fact-checkers rated, and it displays these posts lower in people's News Feeds.

Facebook, which partnered with Carnegie-Mellon University and the University of Maryland on a COVID-19 survey, said that vaccine hesitancy for people in the US on Facebook has declined by 50%. Vaccine acceptance increased by 35% in France, 25% in Indonesia and 20% in Nigeria, the social network said.

The company also shared new data including what domains, links, pages and posts were the most widely viewed in the US on Facebook between April and June. Facebook counts a view when content appears on the News Feed, so the metric differs from engagement. The social network owns data analytics tool CrowdTangle, but executives have reportedly raised concerns about data that shows high engagement with right-wing sites.

"The narrative that has emerged is quite simply wrong," Rosen said, noting that CrowdTangle includes data about interactions from a limited set of certain pages, groups and accounts.

Facebook said the most viewed domain was YouTube. The most viewed link was the Player Alumni Resources, and the top page was from Unicef. The most viewed post was an image from a motivational speaker that asked people about the first words they see in a block of letters.

A Facebook engineer abused access to user data to track down a woman who had left their hotel room after they fought on vacation, new book says

A Facebook engineer abused employee access to user data to track down a woman who had left him after they fought, a new book said.

This story is available exclusively to Business Insider subscribers. Become an Insider and start reading now.

Between January 2014 and August 2015, the company fired 52 employees over exploiting user data for personal means, said an advance copy of "An Ugly Truth: Inside Facebook's Battle for Domination" that Insider obtained.

The engineer, who is unnamed, tapped into the data to "confront" a woman with whom he had been vacationing in Europe after she left the hotel room they had been sharing, the book said. He was able to figure out her location at a different hotel.

Another Facebook engineer used his employee access to dig up information on a woman with whom he had gone on a date after she stopped responding to his messages. In the company's systems, he had access to "years of private conversations with friends over Facebook messenger, events attended, photographs uploaded (including those she had deleted), and posts she had commented or clicked on," the book said. Through the Facebook app the woman had installed on her phone, the book said, the engineer was also able to see her location in real time.

Facebook employees were granted user data access in order to "cut away the red tape that slowed down engineers," the book said.

"There was nothing but the goodwill of the employees themselves to stop them from abusing their access to users' private information," wrote Sheera Frenkel and Cecilia Kang, the book's authors. They added that most of the employees who abused their employee privileges to access user data only looked up information, although a few didn't stop there.

Most of the engineers who took advantage of access to user data were "men who looked up the Facebook profiles of women they were interested in," the book said.

Facebook told Insider it fired employees found to have accessed user data for nonbusiness purposes.

"We've always had zero tolerance for abuse and have fired every single employee ever found to be improperly accessing data," a spokesperson told Insider in a statement. "Since 2015, we've continued to strengthen our employee training, abuse detection, and prevention protocols. We're also continuing to reduce the need for engineers to access some types of data as they work to build and support our services."

A problem that cropped up 'nearly every month'

Mark Zuckerberg, Facebook's CEO, was first made aware of the problem in September 2015, when Alex Stamos, Facebook's chief security officer at the time, raised the issue with him. In a presentation to Zuckerberg and the company's top executives, Stamos said engineers had abused the access "nearly every month," the book said.

At the time, more than 16,000 employees had access to users' private data, the book said. Stamos suggested tightening access to fewer than 5,000 employees and fewer than 100 for particularly sensitive information such as passwords. He proposed requiring employees to submit formal requests for access to private data but received pushback from executives. Zuckerberg said changes on the matter were "a top priority" and tasked Stamos with finding a solution and giving an update in a year, the book said.

But changes that would limit data retention were "antithetical to Mark's DNA," one employee told the book's authors.

The employee added, "At various times in Facebook's history there were paths we could have taken, decisions we could have made, which would have limited, or even cut back on, the user data we were collecting," Frenkel and Kang wrote. "Even before we took those options to him, we knew it wasn't a path he would choose."

Following recent U.S. Food and Drug Administration actions to support test development, the FDA took swift action this week to get more tests for screening asymptomatic individuals on the market. Today, the agency authorized several tests for over-the-counter (OTC) use without a prescription when used for serial screening. In addition to the tests authorized for OTC use, one serial screening test was authorized for use in a point-of-care (POC) setting without a prescription, and an additional screening test was authorized for POC use with a prescription. The addition of the OTC and POC tests for screening will give schools, workplaces, communities and others several options for serial screening tests that are accurate and reliable. These authorizations follow the FDA’s recent actions to advance OTC and other screening test development.

“Screening testing, especially with the over-the-counter tests authorized today, is an important part of the country’s pandemic response—many schools, workplaces, communities, and other entities are setting up testing programs to quickly screen for COVID-19. With the FDA’s authorization of multiple tests, the public can be assured these tests have met our scientific standards for emergency use authorization. As we’ve said all along, if it’s a good test, we’ll authorize it,” said Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health. “The FDA has taken many steps to support test development throughout the pandemic, including authorizing tests quickly, offering many avenues for test developers to work with us to get their tests on the market, if shown to be accurate and reliable, and issuing enforcement policies for COVID-19 tests. As the pandemic has progressed, we have worked with test developers wishing to add screening claims.”

In total, the FDA has authorized three tests with serial screening claims (testing asymptomatic individuals multiple times on a routine basis). Specific tests authorized this week:

Quidel QuickVue At-Home OTC COVID-19 test - authorized for OTC at-home serial screening

Abbott BinaxNOW (multiple configurations) Abbott BinaxNOW COVID-19 Antigen Self Test – authorized for OTC at-home serial screening Abbott BinaxNOW COVID-19 Ag Card 2 Home Test - authorized for OTC at-home serial screening with telehealth proctor Abbott BinaxNOW COVID-19 Ag 2 Card – authorized for POC serial screening without a prescription

BD Veritor System for Rapid Detection of SARS-CoV-2 – authorized for POC serial screening with a prescription

These tests had been previously authorized by the agency (some under different names) to test those with COVID-19 symptoms, but the actions this week authorize testing of asymptomatic individuals when used for serial testing.

These authorizations follow the agency’s multiple steps to streamline the process for test developers interested in authorization for screening with serial testing to increase consumer access to testing, as well as information the FDA has issued to help schools, workplaces, communities, and others establish screening programs.

The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, products that give off electronic radiation, and for regulating tobacco products.

NIH Initiates Clinical Trial to Study Mixed Booster COVID-19 Vaccine Regimens

BETHESDA, MD – The National Institutes of Health (NIH) has commenced a Phase 1/2 clinical trial to assess the safety and immunogenicity of mixed booster COVID-19 vaccine regimens, funded and led by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), a component of the NIH. This groundbreaking trial aims to prepare for potential booster shots due to waning immunity and the evolution of the virus.

Dr. Anthony S. Fauci, NIAID Director, stated, "As we continue to build on our understanding of COVID-19 vaccine immunity, this trial will allow us to explore key questions about optimizing vaccine protocols, especially in the context of variant viruses. A mixed vaccine regimen may be an important approach for booster shots."

The mix-and-match trial, named "Study of the Effectiveness of Additional Heterologous Doses of COVID-19 Vaccines (Seasonal Coronavirus Vaccines Trial)," includes three U.S. sites. In the first stage of the trial, 150 participants who have completed one of the three FDA Emergency Use Authorized (EUA) COVID-19 vaccines will receive a booster dose of the Moderna mRNA-1273 vaccine. Additional cohorts will include participants who are initially unvaccinated against SARS-CoV-2 and will receive the two-dose Moderna vaccine regimen.

Dr. Robert L. Atmar, M.D., Principal Investigator at Baylor College of Medicine, shared his enthusiasm for the trial: "We are grateful for this opportunity to help answer crucial questions about COVID-19 vaccines. We eagerly anticipate enrolling participants and hope that our research can inform public health policy and improve global health."

The adaptive design of the trial will allow for new arms to be introduced as additional vaccines receive EUA or variant vaccines become available. Trial participants will be followed for up to a year post-vaccination for safety monitoring, side effects, and immune response evaluations.

Dr. Kirsten E. Lyke, M.D., Principal Investigator at the University of Maryland, College Park, highlighted the importance of understanding mixed vaccine schedules: "Our primary goal is to explore whether mixed vaccine schedules generate robust immune responses. We believe that understanding this information is crucial to informing public health policy on booster doses and mixed vaccine schedules."

This trial is part of the NIH's larger effort to address pressing questions about COVID-19 vaccines and will contribute to the ongoing global response to the pandemic. Initial results are expected in late summer 2021, with trial information available on clinicaltrials.gov under identifier NCT04889209.

As the primary federal agency for medical research in the United States, the NIH focuses on understanding the causes of infectious, immune-mediated diseases, and other health conditions. Throughout its rich history, the NIH has led the nation in curing and preventing diseases.

For more information, please visit the NIAID's website at niaid.nih.gov and the NIH's website at nih.gov.

Oxford School Shooting Lawsuit Seeks $100 Million in Damages

Dec 9 (Reuters) – A lawsuit seeking $100 million in damages was filed on Thursday against the Oxford Community School District and its officials for the deadly shooting at Oxford High School in Michigan. The lawsuit accuses the school district of failing to act on prior knowledge of the shooter's threatening behavior, which resulted in the deaths of four students and injuries to seven others, including a teacher.

The lawsuit was filed on behalf of Riley Franz, 17, who was injured in the shooting, and her sister Bella, 14, by Michigan personal injury attorney Geoffrey Fieger. It names the school district's superintendent, Timothy Throne, principal, Steven Wolf, and other staff members as defendants.

"This lawsuit is about holding the Oxford Community School District accountable for its failures that led to the tragic shooting at Oxford High School," Fieger said in a statement. "The school district knew or should have known that the shooter was a danger to himself and others, yet they failed to take any meaningful action to prevent this tragedy."

The lawsuit alleges that the school district was aware of the shooter's disturbing online activity, including threats of violence and an ammunition search, but failed to properly respond. It also accuses the school of assuring parents and students of safety despite knowing of these warning signs.

"The school district's assurances of safety were nothing more than empty words," Fieger said. "They knew or should have known that the shooter was a danger, and they failed to take any action to protect our children."

The lawsuit further criticizes the school staff's failure to properly respond to the shooter's threats of violence and ammunition search. It alleges that the school failed to conduct a proper investigation or take any disciplinary action against the shooter, despite the clear warning signs.

"This shooting was entirely preventable," Fieger said. "The school district had a duty to protect our children, and they failed miserably."

The lawsuit comes as the shooter's parents, James and Jennifer Crumbley, are facing involuntary manslaughter charges for providing their son with a gun and ignoring warning signs. The parents are accused of failing to properly secure the gun and ignoring their son's disturbing behavior, including threats of violence.

The Oxford Community School District has not yet responded to the lawsuit.

Trump Acquitted in Second Impeachment Trial, Highlighting Divisive Legacy

WASHINGTON (AP) – Former President Donald Trump has once again escaped conviction in an impeachment trial, this time for inciting an insurrection at the U.S. Capitol on January 6. The vote to acquit was 57-43, falling short of the two-thirds majority required in the Senate.

Trump, the only president to be impeached twice, faced his first impeachment in 2019 over a controversial phone call with the Ukrainian president, a trial that delved into intricate evidence and testimony. The second impeachment, however, was more visceral, with senators acting as eyewitnesses to the violence that unfolded at the Capitol.

Sen. Chuck Schumer, the Democratic majority leader, emphasized the gravity of the charges, stating, "The former president summoned the mob, assembled the mob, and lit the flame of this attack. Everything that followed was his doing."

Senate Republican leader Mitch McConnell, while acknowledging Trump's role in the events, ultimately voted to acquit on constitutional grounds. In a post-trial speech, McConnell criticized the former president's actions, saying, "There's no question – none – that President Trump is practically and morally responsible for provoking the events of the day."

The unprecedented nature of the trial saw senators reliving the harrowing experience of the insurrection, with Trump's rhetoric and encouragement of his followers central to the impeachment charge. His ability to avoid consequences, even in the face of such dramatic events, raised questions about the limits of presidential power.

Trump, who refrained from public comments during the trial, maintained a significant level of loyalty among his congressional supporters. His influence on his base was compared to a previous boast, where he claimed he could shoot someone on Fifth Avenue and still not lose voters.

Despite the violence and the second impeachment, Trump's loyal following in Congress stood by him, underscoring the deep political divisions in the country. The acquittal underscores the challenge faced by lawmakers in holding the former president accountable for his actions.

In his closing arguments, House impeachment manager Rep. Jamie Raskin implored senators to consider the long-term implications of their vote, saying, "If this is not impeachable, then nothing is impeachable."

As the trial came to a close, the Senate's failure to secure a conviction left many Americans wondering about the future of accountability for a former president and the potential consequences of incendiary political rhetoric. Trump's legacy remains divisive, with his actions and words continuing to shape the nation's political landscape.

Monica Gandhi, Professor of Medicine and Associate Division Chief of the Division of HIV, Infectious Diseases, and Global Medicine at the University of California San Francisco at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center, emphasizes the importance of getting vaccinated: "The COVID-19 vaccines have undergone rigorous clinical trials and have been authorized for emergency use only after demonstrating strong safety and efficacy."

Megan Ranney, Emergency Medicine Physician and Founding Director of the Brown-Lifespan Center for Digital Health at Brown University, adds: "The benefits of the COVID-19 vaccines far outweigh the risks. Millions of people have been vaccinated without any major safety concerns."

Despite these assurances, vaccine hesitancy persists due to concerns about new variants and potential side effects. Alessandro Sette, an immunologist at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology, explains, "While new variants are a concern, the current vaccines are effective against the major ones. Matthew Frieman, Associate Professor of Microbiology and Immunology at the University of Maryland School of Medicine, emphasizes the importance of vaccines in reducing virus transmission, including asymptomatic transmission: "Vaccines not only protect the individual but also contribute to herd immunity, which can help us return to normal activities."

Sette explains, "The rapid development of new vaccines and technology allows us to adapt quickly to new variants. Frieman concludes, "Vaccines, coupled with public health measures, are our best chance at ending the pandemic. It's crucial that we address vaccine hesitancy and encourage everyone to get vaccinated to protect themselves and their communities."

In conclusion, experts assure the safety and efficacy of COVID-19 vaccines amidst concerns about new variants and potential side effects. Zabihullah Mujahid, Taliban spokesman, announced that the Taliban had taken control of the Presidential Palace in Kabul, with the transition broadcast live by Al Jazeera. Mujahid said: "The process of transferring power has started. We will announce a new government soon."

Blinken, speaking to reporters at the State Department, defended the decision to destroy documents before leaving the embassy. He said: "Document destruction is standard procedure in such situations."

The Taliban's takeover of Kabul came after a lightning offensive that saw them capture major cities across the country in just a few days. The insurgent group had been gaining territory for months as US and NATO forces withdrew from Afghanistan.

Blinken acknowledged the challenges of the evacuation, saying: "This is a complex operation, and it will take time. We will continue to work closely with our allies and partners to ensure the safety of US citizens, SIV applicants, and other vulnerable Afghans."

Mckenzie emphasized the need for caution, saying: "We are preparing for the potential for a large-scale airlift to get American citizens out of Afghanistan, and we'll be prepared to do that in a safe and orderly fashion."

Jesuit Priest Under Investigation for Alleged Misconduct

SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) – Rev. Kevin O'Brien, a Jesuit priest who presided over President Joe Biden's inaugural Mass, is under investigation for unspecified allegations, Santa Clara University announced Thursday. O'Brien, who has a long history with the Biden family, has been placed on leave from his position as president of the university amid the investigation.

In a statement, John M. Sobrato, the board chairman of Santa Clara University, said that the allegations against O'Brien involve "behaviors in adult settings, consisting primarily of conversations," which may have violated Jesuit protocols. The nature of the allegations has not been specified publicly.

Tracey Primrose, spokeswoman for the Jesuits West Province, which oversees the investigation, emphasized that Jesuits adhere to a professional code of conduct and are expected to maintain appropriate boundaries in all interactions.

O'Brien, who joined the Society of Jesus in 1996 and was ordained in 2006, has been a prominent figure in the Jesuit community. He has known the Biden family for about 15 years and has presided over services for Biden's vice president inaugurations.

Santa Clara University, where O'Brien served as president, is a top-ranked Jesuit institution with about 5,500 undergraduate students. The university has not made public comments regarding the investigation.

O'Brien and the Jesuits West Province have also not made any public comments about the investigation. It is not clear how long the investigation will take or what the consequences might be for O'Brien if the allegations are found to be true.

The investigation comes at a time when the Catholic Church is facing increased scrutiny over its handling of sexual misconduct allegations. In recent years, several high-profile cases have raised questions about the church's ability to police itself and protect its members from abuse.

The allegations against O'Brien have sparked concern among members of the Santa Clara University community, who are eagerly awaiting the outcome of the investigation.

"We take any allegation of misconduct very seriously and will cooperate fully with the investigation," Sobrato said in his statement. "We will do everything we can to ensure that our campus remains a safe and respectful environment for all members of our community."

The investigation is a reminder that even respected religious leaders can face allegations of misconduct, and that no institution is immune to scrutiny. As the Catholic Church continues to grapple with issues of accountability, cases like O'Brien's will continue to draw attention and raise questions about the church's ability to protect its members.

In the meantime, the Santa Clara University community will wait anxiously for the outcome of the investigation, hoping that it will bring clarity and resolution to the allegations against O'Brien.

Winter Storm Uri Raises Questions About Climate Change and Extreme Cold Events

Winter Storm Uri brought unprecedented cold and extreme weather across the United States, especially affecting states like Texas that are unaccustomed to such severe conditions. The cold snap led to massive spikes in energy demand, overwhelming the power grid and leaving millions of people without electricity during a critical time. As the nation grapples with the aftermath of the storm, the debate among scientists over the role of climate change in such extreme cold events has been reignited.

According to Walt Meier, a Senior Research Scientist at the National Snow and Ice Data Center at the University of Colorado Boulder, the issue of whether climate change influences extreme cold events is a point of contention among scientists. Some researchers argue that global warming could potentially decrease the likelihood of such events, while others suggest that the warming in the Arctic may lead to more frequent cold spells moving further south.

Karin Gleason, a Climate Scientist at the National Centers for Environmental Information at NOAA, points out that complex factors such as sudden stratospheric warming and variations in the Arctic Oscillation played significant roles in shaping the recent cold weather patterns. The Arctic, in particular, is warming at a rate almost twice as fast as the rest of the planet, raising concerns about its impact on extreme weather patterns in the future.

Jennifer Francis, a Senior Scientist at the Woodwell Climate Research Center, highlights that the current cold event aligns with predictions that extreme weather events, both hot and cold, may become more common in a warming climate. She emphasizes that the meandering jet stream can create conditions where extreme heat and cold coexist, leading to unpredictable and severe weather patterns.

Francis underscores the importance of considering the broader context of climate change when assessing individual weather events. "We need to look at the bigger picture and how these extreme events fit into the overall trend of a changing climate," she says. The warming Arctic, she adds, can disrupt the jet stream, potentially leading to more persistent weather patterns that result in prolonged cold spells.

On the other hand, James Screen, an Associate Professor of Climate Science at the University of Exeter, expresses skepticism about directly linking climate change to an increase in extreme cold events. Screen highlights the complexities of atmospheric dynamics and the need for further research to establish a clearer understanding of the relationship between climate change and extreme weather occurrences.

As communities affected by Winter Storm Uri work to recover and rebuild, the conversation about the intersection of climate change and extreme weather events continues to evolve. While the exact influence of climate change on extreme cold events remains a subject of debate, one thing is clear: the need for comprehensive research and preparedness to address the challenges of a changing climate is more urgent than ever.

Twitter Permanently Bans @realDonaldTrump Account After Pro-Trump Riot at Capitol

WASHINGTON (AP) – In a historic move, Twitter permanently suspended the account of former President Donald Trump on Friday, citing concerns of further incitement of violence following a pro-Trump mob's assault on the U.S. Capitol. The account, which had more than 57,000 tweets, was a significant tool for Trump's direct communication with the public.

"After close review of recent Tweets from the @realDonaldTrump account and the context around them we have permanently suspended the account due to the risk of further incitement of violence," Twitter Safety said in a statement.

The suspension came after a mob of Trump supporters stormed the Capitol building on January 6, 2021, in an attempt to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election. Five people died as a result of the violence.

Peter Costanzo, an online marketing director who helped Trump join Twitter in 2009, suggested the @realDonaldTrump handle. "He was very excited about it," Costanzo told The Associated Press. "He loved the idea of being able to communicate directly with his supporters."

Trump used the platform extensively during his presidency, often bypassing official media channels. His messages ranged from promotional posts to attacks on political opponents and controversial statements. In his final months on the platform, Twitter flagged 471 of Trump's tweets for misinformation.

Sam Nunberg, a former Trump adviser, said Trump's Twitter account was a critical part of his political strategy. "He used it to go around the mainstream media and speak directly to his supporters," Nunberg said. "It was a game changer."

Trump's account was used to announce major decisions and insults alike. In 2017, he used Twitter to announce the United States' withdrawal from the Paris climate accord. In 2019, he used the platform to attack Democratic congresswomen, calling them the "Squad" and telling them to "go back" to their countries of origin.

Former President Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., criticized Twitter for banning his father's account while allowing leaders of authoritarian regimes to remain on the platform. "They're allowing dictators and authoritarians to use their platform to spread propaganda and lies, but they ban American citizens," Trump Jr. told Fox News.

Historians may look back on @realDonaldTrump's tweets as a window into Trump's thoughts and presidency. "These tweets provide a unique insight into the mind of a president and the way he communicated with the American people," said Julian Zelizer, a professor of history and public affairs at Princeton University. "They will be an important part of the historical record."

Suez Canal shutdown shows the vulnerability of the global economy to extreme events

A critical global shipping node – Egypt’s Suez Canal – was reopened on Monday, March 29, six days after being shut down when the 400-meter-long container ship Ever Given became lodged in the canal. A statement by the Suez Canal Authority initially blamed the incident on high winds and a sand storm that reduced visibility, but later said that strong winds were “not the only cause,” and that an investigation was ongoing.

There is no clear indication at this point that climate change played a role in the sandstorm that led to the ship’s blocking the canal, but the incident raises intriguing questions that likely will prompt research into any correlation.

The multi-day shutdown of one of the world’s busiest shipping chokepoints underscores the vulnerability of the global food system and economy to disruptions. That vulnerability is playing on the stage of increasingly extreme weather, rising seas, and an increasingly just-in-time world of shipping.

Figure 1. MODIS satellite image from March 23, 2021, the day of the grounding of the container ship Ever Given in the Suez Canal. A cold front over Egypt was causing a widespread dust storm that affected the Red Sea, Suez Canal, and waters of the Mediterranean Sea. (Image credit: NASA Worldview)

Meteorology of the event

The high winds and sand storm that contributed to the grounding incident were caused by a cold front trailing to the south of a low-pressure system centered near southern Turkey.

As the cold front swept eastwards across Egypt on March 23, powerful winds of 25-30 knots (29-35 mph) blew along the axis of the Red Sea from the south-southeast, into the southern end of the Suez Canal, as seen in the 6 UTC analysis from the GFS model (Figure 2). The Ever Given became stuck at 05:40 UTC that day. According to the GFS analysis, a sharp wind shift, with winds blowing out of the southwest to west, was present near the spot where the Ever Given blocked the canal, about five miles north of its connection with the Red Sea.

The New York Times reported that winds in excess of 70 mph blew in the region where the Ever Given became stuck; the owner of the ship, BSM, said that “initial investigations suggest the vessel grounded due to strong wind.” The strong winds were accompanied by large amounts of sand and dust, reducing visibility and making navigation more challenging.

Winds this strong are uncommon in the region, but strong winds have delayed shipping traffic or closed the Suez Canal on at least two occasions – December 11, 2010, and February 11, 2015.

Figure 2. The GFS model analysis from 6 UTC March 23, 2021, at the time of the grounding of the Ever Given. Sustained south-southeasterly winds of 25-30 knots (29-35 mph, yellow-green and yellow colors) were blowing across the Red Sea into the entrance of the Suez Canal. The black wind barbs show a sharp wind shift was present near the southern portion of the canal, where the Ever Given became stranded. (Image credit: Tropical Tidbits)

A video Tweeted by Vakrio Technologies showed the course and heading of the Ever Given as it entered the canal, demonstrating that the canal is initially angled from southwest to northeast. Ever Given passed very close to the northwest bank of the canal at the start of its traverse, presumably pushed by the strong south-southeasterly winds blowing into the canal entrance from the Red Sea. For unknown reasons, the vessel was moving at 15 mph, well in excess of the 10 mph speed limit in the canal. As explained in an excellent analysis in the Financial Times (free registration required) by Brendan Greely, when a ship gets too close to a bank, shallow-water hydrodynamic forces can act to spin the boat – a well-known phenomenon known as the bank effect, where the water speeds up between the boat and the bank, the pressure drops, and the stern is pulled into the bank while the bow is pushed away from shore. Possibly because of the bank effect, the Ever Given then slewed close to the opposite (east) bank of the canal. At that point, the canal is oriented north-south, and the vessel angled its heading to the left, perhaps again due to the bank effect, or possibly in response to a crosswind that had developed due to a wind shift to a more westerly direction. The ship again came close to the west (left) bank, potentially because of a swirling wind that briefly blew from the south, reducing the cross-wind component that was pushing the boat to the right. The Ever Given finally ran aground with its stern on the west bank of the canal and its bow on the east bank (Figure 3), suggesting that the bank effect may have acted to spin the ship and lodge it in the canal when it came too close to the west bank.

Figure 3. Sentinel-2 satellite image of the Ever Given stuck in the Suez Canal on March 24, 2021. The stern of the ship was lodged against the west bank of the canal. (Photo credit: Pierre Markuse)

Near-record March heat preceded the March 23 sandstorm

An extraordinary March heat wave preceded the cold front and sandstorm that contributed to the canal-blocking incident; the day previously, Kharga, Egypt, recorded a scorching temperature of 44 degrees Celsius (111.2°F), just 0.2 degrees Celsius below the highest March temperature ever recorded in the nation, according to weather records expert Maximiliano Herrera. The day of the sandstorm (March 23), Luxor, Egypt, hit 43.6 degrees Celsius – just 0.6 degrees Celsius below the March national record. Herrera documented that on the day after the sandstorm, Mitribah, Kuwait hit 44.6 degrees Celsius (112.3°F) – the hottest temperature ever recorded in the Arabian Peninsula in March.

Extreme heat dries the soil, allowing winds to more readily mobilize sand grains and create a dust storm. For example, a study of a high-impact sandstorm over the Middle East during August-September 2015 found that unusually hot and dry conditions preceding the event were responsible for its near-record intensity.

“The simulations showed that what was very unique about this storm is that, first, it was preceded by a very hot period, and so the land that was not covered with vegetation would be drier and it would be easier to entrain sand grains from it,” said study co-author Eli Bou-Zeid, in an interview with the Climate News Network.

Similarly, when the strong cold front swept through Egypt on March 23, 2021, the winds behind the front were able to loft an unusual amount of dust and sand into the air because of the earlier hot conditions. That created difficult circumstances for navigation on the Suez Canal. Climate change is increasing the incidence of such extreme heat events, and may have played a role in the blockage of the Suez Canal if reduced visibility is determined to have played a role in the ship’s grounding.

Figure 4. The GFS model analysis from 6 UTC March 23, 2021, at the time of the grounding of the Ever Given, showing the departure of temperature from average. Temperatures were as much as 20 degrees Celsius (36°F) above average to the east of a cold front moving across Egypt. (Image credit: Tropical Tidbits)

Wind a more likely culprit than poor visibility

Wind appears to be the main culprit for the grounding of the ship, however, with the sandstorm’s strong and variable winds making it more difficult to navigate the passage. For now at least, it’s speculative whether climate change may have increased the odds of the strong wind event on March 23.

However, the large-scale weather pattern responsible for the sandstorm was quite extreme, and climate change could have contributed to make this event more extreme. Observations of the upper-level air patterns at 500 millibars (about 18,000 feet) on that date showed a very amplified and wavy jet stream pattern, with a strong ridge of high pressure over the Middle East and a strong trough of low pressure just to its west over the central Mediterranean Sea (Figure 5). Both features were about two standard deviations from the mean.

There has been a sharp increase in similar “global weirding” extreme jet stream patterns in summer, as a result of a phenomenon known as quasi-resonant amplification or “QRA” – described in detail in an October 2018 realclimate.org post by Michael Mann and reported in this writer’s 2018 post at Weather Underground. Modeling studies have shown that climate change may be responsible for the observed increase in summer QRA events, potentially because of how the Arctic is warming up more than twice as fast as the planet overall. A March 2021 study, “Large scale connection to deadly Indian heat waves” found that QRA events can also occur in spring, and may be connected to deadly April and May heat waves that affected India in 2010-2015.

But Dr. Stefan Rahmstorf, a co-author of the 2018 QRA study, wrote in an email that there was no evidence of QRA conditions during the week leading up to the Suez Canal sandstorm on March 23. Dr. Mann, lead author of the 2018 QRA study, added, “Our work certainly supports the increased incidence of persistent weather extremes of this sort (in fact, there’s a new study just out that further confirms that these events are indeed increasing in Europe during the warm season), so the connection is plausible but not confirmed.” Thus, it is possible that climate change may have increased the odds of the unusually amplified jet stream pattern responsible for the March 23 wind event in Egypt, but this possibility is speculative, and only more research may lead to further understanding of a possible connection with a changing climate.

Figure 5. Northern Hemisphere 500-millibar heights (in decameters, or tens of meters) from the GFS model analysis from 6 UTC March 23, 2021, at the time of the grounding of the Ever Given. Colors show how much the predicted 500-mb height deviates from the average for this time of year, in standard deviations. Ridges of high pressures are shown in orange, and troughs of low pressure are blue; Egypt was located at the boundary between a strong trough of low pressure and strong ridge of high pressure. (Image credit: Tropical Tidbits)

Climate change increasingly likely to threaten global trade chokepoints

While the connections to climate change of the grounding of the Ever Given and closure of the Suez Canal are speculative, the event serves as a warning that climate change can be expected to cause an increase in extreme events that will impact critical global trade chokepoints. As explained in a 2017 report from Chatham House, much of the food required to feed 2.8 billion people passes through 14 critical shipping chokepoints (Figure 6): maritime corridors such as straits and canals, coastal infrastructure in major crop-exporting regions, and inland transport infrastructure in major crop-exporting regions. These chokepoints are at risk of closure due to three factors:

1) Extreme weather events or sea level rise;

2) Security and conflict hazards from war, political instability, piracy, organized crime and/or terrorism; and

3) Decisions by authorities to close a chokepoint or restrict the passage of food (for example, by imposing export controls).

Thirteen of the 14 critical chokepoints have had a closure or interruption in transit at least once between 2002-2017, with the Strait of Gibraltar the only exception. Many of these events had potential climate change connections: for example, the 2011 and 2012 heat waves in the U.S. that led to multiple derailments of trains where railroad tracks warped in excessive heat.

Figure 6. Key global chokepoints for shipping. (Image credit: Chatham House, adapted from Rodrigue, J.-P., Comtois, C. and Slack, B., 2017, “The Geography of Transport Systems,” New York: Routledge

The report explained, “Climate change is increasing the threat of disruption by acting as a hazard multiplier across all three categories of chokepoint risk. It will increase the frequency and severity of extreme weather, leading to more regular closures of chokepoints and greater wear and tear on infrastructure. Rising sea levels will threaten the integrity of port operations and coastal storage infrastructure, and will increase their vulnerability to storm surges. Climate change is expected to aggravate drivers of conflict and instability. It will also lead to more frequent harvest failures, increasing the risk of governments imposing ad hoc export controls.”

The forced closure of the Suez Canal due to a possibly climate change-related event should act as a warning: Climate change will cause disruptions to critical global trade chokepoints more frequently in the coming years, and we need to take strong actions to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases and reduce vulnerabilities to chokepoint disruptions.

Tiger Woods in Critical Condition After Devastating Car Accident

Golfing World in Shock as Beloved Icon Battles for Recovery

Los Angeles, California - The sporting world is reeling in shock and concern following the news of Tiger Woods' involvement in a serious car accident on Tuesday morning. The legendary golfer was rushed to the hospital with severe leg injuries and is currently undergoing surgery.

The incident occurred in the upscale community of Rancho Palos Verdes, California, where Woods resides. According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, Woods' vehicle veered off the road and struck a tree, resulting in significant damage. Firefighters and paramedics were required to extricate Woods from the wreckage.

Woods, who was in Los Angeles for the PGA Tour's Genesis Invitational, had just completed his role in the tournament's trophy presentation ceremony. The golfing community, including PGA Tour Commissioner Jay Monahan and fellow golfer Max Homa, expressed their support and prayers for Woods' speedy recovery.

"Tiger Woods is a global icon and his contributions to the sport of golf are immeasurable," Monahan said. "We are all incredibly concerned about his well-being and will continue to offer our support to him and his family during this difficult time."

Homa, who had the privilege of playing alongside Woods in the Genesis Invitational Pro-Am, echoed these sentiments. "Tiger is a true legend and an inspiration to us all," Homa said. "Our thoughts are with him and we wish him a full and speedy recovery."

The outpouring of support extended beyond the golfing world, with celebrities from various fields expressing their concern and well-wishes for Woods. Lindsey Vonn, LeBron James, and Alex Rodriguez were among those who took to social media to share their prayers and encouragement.

Prior to the accident, Woods had been engaged in a two-day shoot with Golf Digest/Golf TV, where he was joined by celebrities such as Jada Pinkett Smith and Dwyane Wade. Daniel Rapaport, a writer for Golf Digest, described Woods as being in high spirits during the shoot.

"Tiger was in a great mood and seemed to be really enjoying himself," Rapaport said. "He was joking around with Jada and Dwyane, and they all seemed to be having a great time."

The day before the crash, Woods had taken to the golf course with comedian David Spade and actress Jada Pinkett Smith. Woods expressed his delight in the experience, saying, "It was a lot of fun playing with David and Jada. They're both really good athletes and they made it a really enjoyable day."

It is worth noting that Woods had recently undergone a microdiscectomy procedure in January to address a pinched nerve. Despite this recent surgery, Woods had expressed optimism about his participation in the upcoming Masters tournament, although he acknowledged uncertainty about his recovery timeline.

Woods has faced his share of challenges in the past, including a car crash in 2009 and an arrest under suspicion of DUI in 2017. Each time, Woods has addressed these incidents publicly and taken responsibility for his actions.

As the golfing world and beyond await news of Woods' condition, the collective hope is for a full and speedy recovery for one of the most iconic athletes of our time.

Brady's Impactful Speech, Fournette's Admiration Lead Buccaneers to Super Bowl Victory

As the Tampa Bay Buccaneers emerged victorious in Super Bowl LV, defeating the Kansas City Chiefs 31-9, it was clear that the team's success was not solely due to individual talent. According to Leonard Fournette, the Buccaneers running back, a powerful pregame speech delivered by Tom Brady served as a potent message of motivation, focusing on the importance of playing for honor and the significance of players' last names.

"Tom's speech was incredibly impactful," Fournette said. "He talked about the importance of playing for something bigger than ourselves, and how our last names represent our families and the sacrifices they've made for us. It was a powerful reminder of why we play this game."

Brady, a six-time champion with the New England Patriots, secured his seventh title in his 10th Super Bowl appearance, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history. However, it was not just Brady's on-field talent that led to the Buccaneers' victory. Throughout the week leading up to the Super Bowl, Brady sent positive texts to his teammates every morning, boosting their morale and solidifying their focus.

"Tom's texts were incredible," Fournette said. "He always finds a way to lift us up and remind us of why we're here. It's special to play alongside someone like him, and I feel lucky to have had the opportunity to learn from him."

Fournette, who signed with the Buccaneers before the season started, played a key role in the playoffs, scoring important touchdowns, including one in the Super Bowl. Despite contemplating his free agency, Fournette expressed openness to staying in Tampa, indicating the team's intention to aim for another successful season.

"The Buccaneers have a lot of potential, and I'm excited to see what we can do next year," Fournette said. "The organization has shown a commitment to winning, and I believe we can run it back in 2021."

The speech and overall determination led by Brady were pivotal in solidifying the team's focus and drive for the Super Bowl victory. As the Buccaneers celebrated their championship, it was clear that the team's success was not just due to individual talent, but also the collective effort and determination of each player.

"Tom's speech and leadership were huge for us," Fournette said. "He's a true leader, and it's an honor to play for him."

In conclusion, the Buccaneers' Super Bowl victory was not just a testament to Brady's on-field talent, but also the collective effort and determination of the entire team. As Fournette expressed, the team has potential for more achievements, and with organizational support, they can "run it back" in 2021.

Massive Cargo Ship Blocks Suez Canal, Disrupting Global Trade

A skyscraper-sized container ship, the Ever Given, became wedged across Egypt's Suez Canal on Tuesday, blocking all traffic in the vital waterway. This incident threatens to disrupt a global shipping system already strained by the coronavirus pandemic.

The Panama-flagged ship, carrying cargo between Asia and Europe, ran aground in the narrow canal dividing continental Africa from the Sinai Peninsula. Images show the ship's bow touching the eastern wall, while its stern is lodged against the western wall. Experts say such an event has never happened before in the canal's 150-year history.

Tugboats are attempting to dislodge the Ever Given, but it remains unclear when the canal, through which around 10% of world trade flows, will reopen. One official warned it could take at least two days. Meanwhile, concerns are growing that idling ships could become targets for attacks.

"The Suez Canal will spare no effort to ensure the restoration of navigation and serve the movement of global trade," vowed Lt. Gen. Ossama Rabei, head of the Suez Canal Authority.

The Ever Given's crew of 20 is safe, and there have been no reports of injuries or pollution. The refloating operation was temporarily suspended on Wednesday and will resume early Thursday.

The cause of the grounding remains unclear. GAC, a global shipping and logistics company, said the ship experienced a blackout, but this was denied by Bernhard Schulte Shipmanagement, which manages the Ever Given.

Evergreen Marine Corp., the Taiwanese company operating the ship, stated that strong winds pushed the Ever Given off course as it entered the canal from the Red Sea. However, it remains unclear how winds alone could have moved a fully laden vessel weighing 220,000 tons.

This incident highlights the vulnerability of global trade to unexpected events and the potential for disruptions in critical shipping lanes. The impact on global supply chains and the cost of goods remains to be seen.

WHO Updates COVID-19 Vaccine Recommendations for Children: Prioritizing Older Populations and Those with Comorbidities

The World Health Organization (WHO) acknowledges the increasing authorization of COVID-19 vaccines for use in children, with several vaccines receiving emergency use authorization (EUA) in various countries. As the global vaccination rollout continues, WHO reaffirms its commitment to prioritizing the vaccination of older persons and those with comorbidities, given the greatest burden of COVID-19 remains within these groups.

Children and adolescents typically experience milder symptoms of COVID-19 compared to adults. However, it is essential to recognize that children under the age of five years have a higher risk of diseases with symptoms similar to COVID-19, such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza. Additionally, children and adolescents can develop 'long COVID-19' and a rare but serious condition called Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome Temporally Associated with SARS-CoV-2 (PIMS-TS) or Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) post-infection.

Risk factors for severe COVID-19 in children include older age, obesity, and preexisting conditions, such as chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and neurological conditions. While children and adolescents may be less infectious than adults and older adults, they can still transmit the virus, contributing to the overall spread in communities.

Studies on the role of children and adolescents in COVID-19 transmission have produced mixed results. Some research suggests that children may play a less significant role in transmission compared to adults, while other studies indicate that they can contribute significantly to the spread, particularly in educational and childcare settings. The WHO emphasizes the importance of maintaining preventive measures, such as hand hygiene, mask-wearing, and social distancing, to mitigate the risk of infection and transmission.

The socio-economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and response on children and adolescents is significant. School closures, disrupted education, and decreased access to essential health services can adversely affect children's physical, mental, and emotional well-being. Additionally, children from low-income households and marginalized communities are disproportionately affected by the pandemic's socio-economic consequences.

Evidence suggests that there may be a larger impact of pediatric COVID-19-related fatality in low to middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to healthcare services and vaccines is limited. The WHO calls on governments and international organizations to prioritize resources and support for these countries to ensure equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines and essential healthcare services for children and adolescents. In conclusion, while children and adolescents typically experience milder symptoms of COVID-19, it is crucial to recognize their unique vulnerabilities and the potential consequences of the pandemic on their health and well-being. The WHO remains committed to prioritizing the health and well-being of all populations, including children and adolescents, in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Hospitals in Hurricane-Ravaged Houma Strained by 'Perfect Twin-Demic'

HOUMA, La. (AP) – Amidst the devastation brought by Hurricane Ida, the medical community in Houma faces a different type of peril – an overwhelming surge of COVID-19 patients colliding with the storm's catastrophic aftermath. Leonard J. Chabert Medical Center and Terrebonne General Health System, two hospitals in the heart of the impact zone, confront challenges unlike ever before.

Richard Zuschlag, owner of Acadian Ambulance Service, described the intensity: "This 'perfect twin-demic' has a horrendous impact. It is something I pray we never witness again."

Hurricane Ida wreaked havoc on Chabert Medical Center. Water poured in from the ceiling, and structural damage threatened the facility's integrity. Meanwhile, the hospital was brimming with COVID patients, leaving scant resources for hurricane relief. The severity of patients' conditions and neighboring hospitals filled with COVID patients made evacuation unfeasible.

"Ida was a hell of a storm," said Dr. Chuck Burnell, chief medical officer of Acadian Ambulance. "The real concern is the evacuation of 100 patients, 60 of whom have tested positive for COVID-19. It's a scenario that presents immense difficulty."

Hospitals' staff endured unprecedented mental stress as they pleaded for divine protection during the hurricane while fearing their building could crumble around them. Terrebonne General Health System didn't fare better; its roof buckled, and windows shattered under Ida's wrath.

"Protecting our patients and staff was the upmost priority," Burnell added. "But I cannot deny the added pressure of the storm and the pandemic combined."

The coordinated evacuation mission unfolded post-hurricane. Terrebonne General's ambulances secured travel to Baton Rouge for a portion of their patients, managing the colossal task in phases to safeguard everyone's well-being.

Zuschlag weighed in on the relief efforts: "The medical community's unified response to this predicament underscores their commitment to the community."

As the dust from Ida settles and recovery begins, the unparalleled impact of two concurrent disasters leaves an imprint on a battered yet resilient Houma.

The Rittenhouse Verdict: A Troubling Sign for Self-Defense Laws

The acquittal of Kyle Rittenhouse, the teenager who fatally shot two unarmed individuals during protests in Kenosha, Wisconsin, has sparked intense debate and raised serious questions about the state of self-defense laws in the United States. While Rittenhouse was cleared of all charges, his actions and the subsequent praise he has received as a hero of self-defense by some prominent figures, including former President Donald Trump, have left many deeply troubled.

Critics have pointed out that the celebrations of Rittenhouse as a symbol of standing up against lawlessness ignore the stark reality that he took the lives of two individuals who were unarmed. The case has highlighted deep-rooted issues with how self-defense is interpreted, with concerns that the current legal framework offers too much leeway to armed individuals in determining who they perceive as a threat.

The juxtaposition of Rittenhouse's acquittal with the trial of Ahmaud Arbery's killers further accentuates the inconsistencies in how self-defense claims are scrutinized in the justice system. The differing outcomes in these cases reflect a troubling pattern of unequal justice being meted out based on factors like race and privilege.

One critical aspect that has raised eyebrows is Rittenhouse's own actions following the shootings. His decision not to render aid to Joseph Rosenbaum, whom he had shot, or immediately contact law enforcement adds to the complexity of the moral and legal implications of his actions that fateful night.

In contrast, the bravery of Anthony Huber, who attempted to disarm Rittenhouse and tragically lost his life in the process, deserves recognition. Huber's actions underscore the courage of those who stood up against the armed presence in Kenosha and sought to prevent further harm.

The injury of Gaige Grosskreutz, who was wounded by Rittenhouse, also sheds light on the quickness with which Rittenhouse resorted to using his weapon in a volatile situation. This raises troubling questions about whether the presence of firearms in such circumstances escalates rather than defuses tensions, putting more lives at risk.

Looking ahead, the Rittenhouse verdict sets a dangerous precedent that could embolden individuals to bring firearms to public events under the guise of self-defense, potentially leading to more violent confrontations and tragic outcomes. It underscores the urgent need to reevaluate gun control laws and the standards for self-defense to prevent similar tragedies in the future.

Tightening gun control measures and ensuring that self-defense laws are applied rigorously and fairly can help prevent reckless acts of violence like the one that unfolded in Kenosha. It is crucial that we strive to create a society where conflicts are resolved through dialogue and de-escalation rather than through the barrel of a gun. The Rittenhouse case should serve as a wake-up call to reexamine our values and laws to ensure that justice is truly served for all.

ERCOT Names Interim President and CEO After Winter Storm Controversy

AUSTIN, Texas – In the aftermath of the devastating winter storm that left millions without power and resulted in over 100 deaths, the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) has named Brad Jones as the interim president and CEO, replacing Bill Magness. The move comes after Magness was fired following criticism of ERCOT's handling of the storm.

Jones, who previously worked in senior roles at ERCOT, brings extensive experience in the power grid industry to the position. Most recently, he served as the president of the Independent System Operator (ISO) of New York, where he oversaw the operation of the state's power grid.

The decision to replace Magness comes after a deadly winter storm in February that left millions without power and faced criticism for ERCOT's handling of the storm. The storm led to more than 100 deaths and left millions without power amid freezing temperatures. ERCOT and the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC) faced criticism for their handling of the storm, including underestimating the maximum power demand and overestimating available power generation for severe winter conditions.

Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick called for the resignations of Magness and DeAnn Walker, head of the PUC, while Gov. Greg Abbott has called for reforms in ERCOT's governance. Lawmakers are facing pressure to pass legislation to prevent future power failures.

As Texas prepares for a hotter and drier summer than normal, increasing demands on the power grid, the appointment of Jones as interim president and CEO of ERCOT is seen as a move to restore confidence in the organization. Jones has a deep understanding of the power grid and the challenges it faces, and his appointment is expected to help ERCOT navigate the upcoming summer season.

In a statement, Jones expressed his gratitude for the opportunity to serve as interim president and CEO of ERCOT. "I am honored to take on this role during this critical time for ERCOT and the state of Texas," he said. "I look forward to working with the ERCOT team and our stakeholders to ensure the reliable operation of the power grid and prevent future power failures."

The appointment of Jones as interim president and CEO of ERCOT is seen as a positive step towards rebuilding trust in the organization and ensuring the reliable operation of the power grid. As Texas enters the summer season, the power grid will face increased demands, and the appointment of Jones is expected to help ERCOT navigate these challenges.

A Legacy of Service versus a Legacy of Self: Trump's Disparaging Remarks on Powell’s Death Underscore a Lack of Decency

In the wake of Colin Powell's death on October 18, resulting from complications due to COVID-19, the outpouring of grief and remembrance from leaders across the political spectrum reflects the deep respect the former Secretary of State commanded. Powell, a pioneering figure in American military and political leadership, and a critic of Donald Trump, is rightly lauded for his service and integrity. However, Trump's response to Powell's passing starkly deviates from this chorus of praise, underlining yet again the former president's evident deficiency in decency and respect.

Trump's statement, loaded with tasteless remarks and disrespectful jibes, highlighted what he considered Powell's mistakes, pejoratively branding the highly esteemed general a “RINO” (Republican In Name Only). This reaction starkly contrasts with the admiration and gratitude expressed by others, from presidents to the general public, who have chosen to honor Powell's legacy and service to the nation. Trump's disdain not only demonstrates a shocking lack of empathy but also reiterates his pattern of attacking Republican leaders who dare to criticize him, further fracturing party unity.

This is not the first time Trump has shown disdain for those who served. His previous attacks on war heroes, most notably the late Senator John McCain, underscore a troubling pattern of belittlement and disrespect towards individuals who sacrificed for their country. In comparison to Powell—a man of principle, intellect, and patriotism—Trump’s actions present the image of a draft dodger, failed businessman, and grifter, far removed from the ideals of service and duty.

Powell's tenure was certainly not without its controversies, most notably his role in presenting the case for the Iraq invasion, a decision he later deeply regretted. Yet, unlike Trump, Powell demonstrated the capacity to admit fault and learn from his mistakes. His willingness to own up to his missteps starkly contrasts with Trump’s incessant denial of any wrongdoing, be it his administration’s bungled response to the COVID-19 pandemic or his refusal to accept responsibility for the divisiveness gripping the nation.

Additionally, Trump's obsession with propagating falsehoods about the 2020 election being 'rigged' and his relentless attacks on the media only further tarnish his legacy, painting a picture of a man more concerned with self-preservation than national well-being. Powell, on the other hand, served his country with grace and distinction, embodying values of honesty and morality that deserve respect, not petty attacks from a man who continuously fails to exhibit basic decency.

Colin Powell’s legacy as a dedicated servant of the nation will endure, his contributions and character remaining a beacon for future leaders. In contrast, Trump's response to Powell’s death not only tarnishes his own reputation but also diminishes the office he once held. As the nation reflects on the memory of a true patriot, it's clear that Trump’s legacy—a legacy of self rather than service—will never measure up. In this moment of mourning, decency dictates that we honor Powell’s service and sacrifice, recognizing the profound disparity between a life dedicated to national service and one consumed by personal vendettas and self-interest.

Kamala Harris Makes History as First Female, Black, and South Asian Vice President

WASHINGTON (AP) – Kamala Harris shattered multiple glass ceilings Wednesday, becoming the first female, first Black, and first South Asian vice president of the United States.

In her inaugural address at the Lincoln Memorial, Harris hailed the moment as a testament to "American aspiration."

"Today, we mark the swearing-in of the first woman, the first Black woman, the first woman of South Asian descent, and the first daughter of immigrants to hold the second highest office in our land," she said. "And while I may be the first woman in this office, I will not be the last."

Harris was sworn in by Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor, using a Bible that belonged to Thurgood Marshall, the first Black Supreme Court justice. Capitol Police Officer Eugene Goodman, who defended the Capitol during the January 6 insurrection, escorted her to the podium.

Her inauguration is seen as a watershed moment in American history, representing significant progress in both gender and racial equality.

"This is a day of celebration and a day of reflection," said Lateefah Simon, a civil rights advocate and friend of Harris. "It's a reminder of how far we've come, but also how much work we still have to do."

Harris' diverse background is reflective of many Americans' stories, bringing important perspectives to the administration.

"She represents the future of our country," said Elizabeth Shelby, a member of the Alpha Kappa Alpha sorority, of which Harris is also a member. "She's a role model for young girls everywhere, showing them that anything is possible."

Harris presided over the Senate as Vice President for the first time Wednesday, swearing in three new Democratic senators.

Before becoming vice president, Harris served as a Senator from California and ran for the presidency herself.

Her historic inauguration was celebrated by members of the Alpha Kappa Alpha sorority and others across the country.

President Joe Biden mentioned Harris' historic election in his inaugural address, marking it as a sign of progress.

"We have a new vice president who represents the best of our nation," Biden said. "She's a trailblazer, a role model, and an inspiration."

Experts believe Harris' vice presidency will redefine political power in America and stress the significance of Black women's leadership.

"This is a historic moment that will have a lasting impact on our country," said Martha S. Jones, a professor of history at Johns Hopkins University. "Kamala Harris' election is a testament to the power of representation and the importance of diversity in our government."

Harris' inauguration is a reminder that the American dream is still alive and well. It is a day of celebration and a day of hope for a more just and equitable future.

Virginia's Governor's Race: A Temperature Check for National Political Tensions

As the eyes of the nation turn to Virginia, the gubernatorial race between Republican Glenn Youngkin and Democrat Terry McAuliffe has taken on a significance that stretches far beyond the state's borders. Seen as a bellwether for the upcoming 2022 midterms, this contest is a window into the changing tides of American politics. Youngkin, a former private equity executive, has managed to carve out a unique campaign strategy by distancing himself from former President Donald Trump, who endorsed him—yet Youngkin is careful not to alienate the Trump base. “I’m running to unite all Virginians,” Youngkin stated emphatically during a recent rally, seeking to reassure moderates and undecided voters of his independent approach.

With cultural issues dominating the campaign discourse, education has emerged as a linchpin of the debate. Youngkin has harnessed parental concerns and frustrations as key aspects of his platform, particularly around how schools handle discussions of race and gender. On the other hand, McAuliffe, a seasoned political operator and former governor, has focused on his experience and past successes in office. “I don’t think parents should be telling schools what they should teach,” McAuliffe defended in response to Youngkin's stance on educational transparency, illustrating the sharp divide in their approaches. As the election day approaches, the race has tightened significantly, with the FiveThirtyEight polling aggregator giving Youngkin a slight lead just one day out from a highly anticipated showdown. Tensions running high in Loudoun were palpable during a recent campaign event where a Youngkin supporter confronted McAuliffe's team, sparking a tense exchange that underscored the fractious political atmosphere. As both candidates head into the final stretch, the stakes could not be higher. “We know we have to fight for every single vote, especially in places like Loudoun,” Youngkin remarked, emphasizing his recognition of the district's significance.
